<thought>The mass spectrum shows a molecular ion at m/z 224.12, which matches the exact mass of C₁₆H₁₆O. The IR spectrum displays a strong carbonyl stretch around 1723 cm⁻¹ and aromatic C–H stretches, indicating a ketone with aromatic rings. A structure that satisfies C₁₆H₁₆O, contains a carbonyl, and has two phenyl rings is 4‑propyl‑benzophenone (a benzophenone where one phenyl ring bears a propyl group). Its SMILES representation is O=C(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(CCC)cc1, which yields the correct formula C₁₆H₁₆O. This is the most parsimonious structure consistent with the data.</thought>
<final_answer>O=C(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(CCC)cc1</final_answer>
